newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields edge higher, await AIRC.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields edge higher, await AIRC.

text.p: *Futures related selling saw Australian bond yields edge higher during the course of the morning as the market cautiously awaited Tuesday's "living wage" verdict by the AIRC.

Futures related selling saw Australian bond yields edge higher during the course of the morning as the market cautiously awaited Tuesday's "living wage" verdict by the Australian Industrial Relations Commission.

"There's been one main seller on the futures floor this morning, and nobody wants to stand in the way at the moment. The market seems to have run out of steam after last week, but that could easily turn after tomorrow," one trader said.
The market rallied strongly last week in anticipation of the AIRC handing down a moderate wage verdict and that Wednesday's quarterly inflation report will be benign.

"Good inflation numbers and a good outcome on the wage case could give an added impetus in the short term, and we could see a further rally in the bond market," said David Landsley, treasury economist at National Bank of Australia.

Economists forecasts for the wage claim centre on a A$12 per week pay award by AIRC in response to the government's A$8 per week and the Australian Council of Trade Unions A$20 per week and 8.75 percent minimum pay award.
An outcome of around A$12 is not expected to cause the Reserve Bank undue concern as it would keep wages growth within the central bank's 4.0-4.5 percent comfort zone.

The RBA has warned that a decision that pushes wages growth to a rate inconsistent with its 2.0-3.0 percent underlying inflation target would see the central bank take appropriate monetary policy action.
A high pay award would also overshadow any positive implications for the bond market from the expected benign outcome in Wednesday's inflation report.

Median forecasts for the headline CPI centre on a rise of just 0.1 percent for an annual rate of 1.2 percent and the underlying rate up 0.4 percent for 2.1 percent annually, according to a Reuters survey of economists.

The weaker tone saw the local market underperform the dollar bloc and give up almost all the spread narrowing seen last week. U.S. Treasuries firmed on Friday as the market consolidated its recent bear run, while currency considerations saw Canadian bonds underperform the U.S. as the Canadian dollar weakened.
